I have previously cited some related U.K. newspaper
articles, for example:

'Scotsman' Newspaper
24 September, 1997

'Mystery of the Spy that Fell to Earth'
by Annette McCann and Bill Chisholm

A Russian spy satellite was blamed last night for an
outbreak of hysteria stretching from the Western Isles to
the north of England.

As red flaming objects rained down from the skies across
Britain, the extent of the disaster was unclear. In the
Borders it was said to be a plane crash; in Edinburgh it
was a meteorite shower; and in Newcastle they feared
aliens had landed.

[...]

The bright lights travelling at high speed sparked a
full-scale emergency in the Borders when another woman
reported a possible plane crash in Berwickshire, near the
A6105 road.

Louise Aitken Walker, said, 'Everything was silent out on
the moor, then my attention was drawn to a fiery object
the size of a football descending about 300 metres from
me. It completely disappeared ten feet from the ground'.
[END]


>It is the fireball that is the start of the entire saga
>and not the lighthouse (as we now know, this came a bit
>later). Anyone trying to confuse the two and proclaiming
>that lighthouses can't fly does not understand the
>entire sequence of events.

I have to say, excepting the coincidental timing, all
other evidence seems to rule out any obvious connection
between that 'fireball' and those unfamiliar lights first
observed within the forest.

Consider the witness statements taken by Halt:-
Airman First Class John Burroughs:

On the night of 25-26 Dec at around 0300 while on patrol
down at east gate myself and my partner saw lights coming
from the woods due east of the gate. The lights were red
and blue the red one above the blue one and they were
flashing on and off.

Because I've never seen anything like that coming from
the woods before we decided to drive down and see what it
was. We went down east gate road and took a right at the
stop sign and drove down about 10 to 20 yards to where
there is a road that goes into the forest. At the road I
could see a white light shining onto the trees and could
still see the red and blue lights. We decided we better
go call it in so we went back up towards east gate. I was
watching the lights and the white light started coming
down the road that led into the forest. We got to the
gate and called it in.

The whole time I could see the lights and the white light
was almost at the edge of the road and the blue and red
lights were still out in the woods. A security unit was
sent down to the gate and when they got there they could
see it too.
[END]

In short, these lights were reportedly visible for quite
some time and remained so even when a further "security
unit" - Penniston and Cabansag - arrived:-

Staff-Sergeant Jim Penniston:

Received dispatch from CSC to rendezvous with Police 4
A1C Burroughs and Police 5 SSgt Steffans at east gate
Woodbridge. Upon arriving at east gate directly to the
east about 1.5 miles in a large wooded area. A large
yellow glowing light was emitting above the trees (refer
diagram). In the center of the lighted area directly in
the center ground level, there was a red light blinking
on and off 5 to 10 second intervals. And a blue light
that was for the most part steady.
[END]

Master-Sergeant J. D. Chandler:

At approx. 0300 hours, 26 December 1980 while conducting
security checks on RAF Bentwaters, I monitored a radio
transmission from A1C Burroughs, Law Enforcement patrol
on RAF Woodbridge, stating that he was observing strange
lights in the wooded area just beyond the access road,
leading from the east gate at RAF Woodbridge. SSgt
Penniston, Security Supervisor, was contacted and
directed to contact Burroughs at the east gate. Upon
arrival, SSgt Penniston immediately notified CSC that he
too was observing these lights and requested to make a
closer observation.
[END]


As also recently mentioned, Burroughs confirms he did not
see any object or lights descend - his first perception
was, from east gate, suddenly noticing unusual lights
amongst the forest trees.

Although Burroughs, Cabansag and Penniston ultimately
ended up pursuing the beacon from Orford Ness
(Orfordness) lighthouse, much had transpired beforehand,
in their investigation of those red/blue/white lights.

Of course, Penniston's increasingly elaborate tales of
encountering and examining a landed, small, triangular-
shaped craft, became quintessential in publicised
accounts.

The reliability of Penniston's claims, compromised by
subsequent 'hypnotic regression', have already been
exposed.

If I may borrow from a related list topic, I will now
highlight further and alarming, associated, doubts:

Regarding:

>From: Mendoza <Horseman@onetel.net.uk>
>Date: Wed, 1 Oct 03 12:55:35 +0100
>Subject: [UFORL] Re: Rendlesham Theories

Peter Brookesmith wrote:

>Sometimes it helps to be a literary critic. As we've

>among certain segments of the B/W base personnel after
>the kerfuffle of Night One. It doesn't take much of a
>chinese whisper to turn "pictures taken by someone
>chasing the UFO" into "film of the UFO", does it? This
>shouldn't cast doubt on the existence of some film (yes,
>most likely stills), merely on reports of its content.
>Which would be fascinating to see.
Peter,

Expanding on Penniston's stated recollections, from his
1997 interviews with Salley Rayl:

"... we carry cameras for possible terrorist encroachment
of the base. We had them with us anyway, and we started
photographing the craft. A 360 walk-around of it and
examining various parts of the length of the craft and
height, trying to find markings or, you know, some type
of entry system".

"As I was taking notes, I also memorized what was in
front of me for what seemed like hours, but was in fact
only minutes. Finally, I unleashed my camera-case cover
and brought the camera up to focus. The air was electric.
It made my hair and skin feel as if I were surrounded by
static electricity or some type of energy. I began
snapping photo after photo. It was still eerily quiet".

Such a pivotal close encounter...

... or was it.


In a striking new development, according to John
Burroughs:

"Here is a kicker, Penniston did not have a camera out
there!!".


Yet, from my considerable discussions with John, there's
perhaps more fascinating intrigue to events that first
night than ever revealed, with some questions still to be
resolved before I'm responsibly in a position to say
more.

As I've noted, "much had transpired beforehand".

Pilgrims,

Interesting thread:

Tim wrote:

>Something that is commonly overlooked (or not
>mentioned/discussed) in many discussions about
>Rendlesham:The first night, is the appearence of a
>fireball over England about the same time Burroughs was
>reporting that something fell into the woods and thought
>it might be an airplane crash.

There are many instances in the Uk when fireball meteors
have been seen and reported variously as a UFO or
crashing aircraft - emergency services sent out etc etc.

There was one last year (or maybe earlier this year)
in Fermanagh and it was instrcutice to see how some ufologists
tried to forge the raw material into a UFO crash.

The (alleged) Berwyn Mountain UFO crash had some of
its origins in several bright fireball meteors which went over
the UK that night. There are several other UFO events where
fireball meteors have played a pivotal role. The interesting bit
is in how ufologists take the initial report and slowly work it
up into a UFO event. If anyone has any reports of fireball meteors
reported as 'crashing planes' UFOs or anything similar I'd love
to see them.

Happy Trails

Andy

Actually, the beta beam does exist. It is a high speed beam of
electrons produced by a cyclotron. It is very similar to a
lightning stroke. But the problem is that, instead of electrostatic
attraction to Travis's body, it would produce a lightning stroke
back to the UFO, taking just the electrons back.

Electrostatic attraction works over only relatively short distances.
The largest distance I have seen something substantial actually moved
by electrostatic attraction (and due to the mounting, we are cheating
here) was a record changer pickup arm (tracking at 2 grams equivalent
force) being attracted to the next record up on the spindle.

By the way, electrostatic attraction obeys the inverse-square force
law, just like electromagnetic attraction. If Travis had somehow been
attracted to the UFO, he would have accelerated faster and faster,
until he hit it with quite a bit of momentum, just like iron is
accelerated when attracted to a magnet.

There are also the charlatans who turn ordinary science into
gobbledygook to confound the untutored (and as Marilyn vos
Savant said a few weeks ago in her column, they make themselves
look brilliant to those who don't understand what they are
saying).

A few years ago, one faker said that the UFO had "drained his
car battery through the headlights via microwaves." At first, I
thought he was just plain lying. Then I realized that there was
another explanation - he left his headlights on, and the battery
drained down so low that the black body emissions of the
headlights were in the microwave band.

Ruppelt, in his "The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects,"
told of a man who used scientific doubletalk to try to sell the
Air Force three working flying saucers. The saucers were
hovercraft powered by vacuum cleaner motors (which had to be
plugged into a wall socket to work). Anyone got a very
l-o-n-g extension cord?

> >is electro statically drawn into the craft.
>
> Ho, ho, lookie here. We have an unknown mechanism
> nulling *mass* (which persists in existing regardless
> of gravity, aka the cause of *weight*, btw) and some
> "beta beams" which may well also be hypothetical --
> anyone else ever heard of them?

I don't want to sound like I'm endorsing this theory! But by "beta beams"
he is presumably refering to beta radiation, ie electrons (as he notes).
In the early days of nuclear physics, some unknown forms of radiation
were labelled alpha, beta, and gamma rays. Alpha rays were discovered to
be helium nuclei (and hence not rays at all); beta rays, electrons (ditto);
and gamma rays, high energy electromagnetic radiation. Calling electrons
"beta beams" is nowadays somewhat archaic, but neither is it nonsensical.

> For those interested in the workings of Prof?! DeAquino's
> mind, I highly recommend this:
>
> http://users.elo.com.br/~deaquino/Cosmological%20Consequences.pdf
>
> -- especially the final paragraphs. For some reason
> none of the highly original papers by this adornment
> of our age seems to have been published in any of the
> usual academic journals. Obviously a cover-up, the usual
> suppression of genius by the forces of conservatism, etc.

Yes, and although his website claims that his papers are
"archived at the Los Alamos National Laboratories Archive", all
this actually means is that he submitted them to the non-peer-reviewed
preprint server <http://arxiv.org>, where "appearance of a paper is
not intended in any way to convey tacit approval of its assumptions,
methods, or conclusions by any agent". Any crackpot who can write something
that looks like a physics paper can get a paper "archived at ... Los
Alamos" and they frequently do ... (which is not to say that arxiv.org
is not an invaluable resource for real physicists.) It is not
and was never meant to be a subsitute for peer-review, simply a way
to get access to the latest research results without having to
wait for a year or more when it appears in a real journal.

Knowing nothing more of De Aquino than what I've learnt by looking at the site link
posted by sburns and checking a couple of the papers there, and having no axe to
grind whatsoever on the issue of 'UFO propulsion' or anything else other than
objectivity, I feel one or two of the points made by the learned Stook need correcting.

First I note that many of the papers by De Aquino, whatever his demerits, are posted
on arXiv and LANL, which those in the know will recognise are not generally open to
'fruitloops and wackos' but are moderated e-archives exclusive to members of
recognised academic or research instituions or sponsored associates thereof.

Second, electrons are perfectly properly described as 'beta particles', as the erudite
Stook surely knows.

Thirdly, it appears to me that sburns is not at all invoking 'suction' by mystic beams
but the disappointingly pedestrian phenomenon of electrostatic attraction.

Fourthly, the effectiveness of this electrostatic attraction evidently depends on the
ability of De Aquino's speculative technology to nullify mass. At this point we
encounter very subtle questions at the margins of theoretical physics, with which I
doubt the self-assured Stook is much inclined to be bothered so I shall content myself
with the comment that De Aquino's programme to quantise gravitation by a
generalisation of the Hamiltonian action function is in my opinion very interesting,
and not a million miles from notions which I myself hold dear ... but then as a mere
fruitloop what would I know? Perhaps the Stook of Meadowsweet could provide us
with a discussion paper on de Aquino's 'kinetic quantum gravity' as compared with
other loopy attempts to solve this problem, such as supersymmetric string theories or
loop quantum gravity? Then we could have a sensible discussion.
Martin Shough

On Wed, 1 Oct 2003, Todd Lemire wrote:

> I'll be contacting the University of Arizona soon so that I may
> get copies of James McDonald's files regarding the Port Huron
> case.

The university may not have them. In 1976, Paul McCarthy, a
political science PhD candidate at the time, wrote his
dissertation on McDonald's UFO work. He had access to McDonald's
papers through Mrs McDonald, not the university. The dissertation
is online at National Capital Area Skeptics (www.ncas.org) under
the "on-line library" link, and at Sign Historical Group
(www.project1947.com/shg/contact.htm); putting it online was a
joint project. The folks at SHG made face-to-face contact with
McCarthy at the time, and may have maintained that contact.

Also, in case you haven't run across it yet, McDonald's testimony
at the 1968 congressional symposium includes the Port Huron case.
The record of that symposium is also online at NCAS, also under
the "on-line library" link. The symposium table of contents
provides links to each of the cases he cites, both as he grouped
them in his testimony and in chronological order.

My understanding is the beam was blue/green. Two possible ways to
produce this "beam" effect (other than light scattering) is gas
ionization and Cerenkov radiation. Cerenkov radiation involves
superluminal particles and as stated would damage a human.
Atmospheric ionization would have little effect on humans other than
sunburn like skin irritation. An example of atmosphere ionization is
the aurora borealis. High-speed electrons (solar wind) spiral around
the Earth's magnetic field lines (producing synchrotron radiation)
and when drawn down into the Earth's atmosphere at the poles, results
in atmospheric ionization of nitrogen/oxygen. A blue/green color:
http://www.ptialaska.net/~hutch/aurora.html

In accordance with the DeAquino theory (the only plausible theory I
know of), a gravity shield nulls the subject's mass (he becomes
weightless) and the beta beam (electrons) charge the subject and then
is electro statically drawn into the craft.

Something that is commonly overlooked (or not mentioned/discussed) in many
discussions about Rendlesham:The first night, is the appearence of a fireball
over England about the same time Burroughs was reporting that something fell
into the woods and thought it might be an airplane crash. Ian Ridpath deserves
the credit on this one as well as figuring out that Halt had the dates wrong on
his memo based on this bit of information. While there are many who doubt
that Burroughs and company could mistake a fireball for a crashing aircraft, it
is a common error by people not familiar with these events (I remember having
to calm an excited topside watch who saw a fireball arc across the sky one
night and thought it was a missle attack on the sub base!). A recent event in
India brings up this problem again:

<A
HREF="http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/3149404.stm">http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/
hi/south_asia/3149404.stm</A>

Most pertinent is this statement by one witness:

>"I first mistook it for... a crashing aircraft, when I saw the huge fireball
with so much >bright light," said Bandita Das, a housewife.

>"For about 10 seconds, the evening on Saturday got lighted up. I panicked
and took >my kids inside the house."

It is the fireball that is the start of the entire saga and not the
lighthouse (as we now know, this came a bit later). Anyone trying to confuse the two
and proclaiming that lighthouses can't fly does not understand the entire
sequence of events.

Tim Printy

under a high terrorist threat at the time with the Irish
Republican Army (IRA), another terrorist group known as
Black September, and some others, so we used them
frequently as part of our patrol."


The following is a list exclusive and previously
unpublished material from Halt's lecture at the 'UFO
Magazine' conference in Leeds, on 31 July, 1994:

I guess, they take their radios, their flashlights, and
Sgt. Penniston takes, the, uh, 35mm camera. We kept
cameras in front of some of the vehicles so we can record
if there were an incident. Somebody runs to a vehicle
when an airplane or some recruits climb over a fence. We
take pictures. It's always handy to have that facility so
that we can reconstruct for a thorough investigation.

Well, Penniston puts the camera over his shoulder, and
then drives down the East Gate road, then intersects the
service road, paved road and the, uh, caravan site or
something at the far end of it. Goes out the back l5O or
2OO feet, turns down into the forest, watching this
object all the time, and go about as far as they can get
without the vehicle, without risk of getting stuck.

[...]

The next day, unbeknownst to me, Captain Mike Verano, the
number three guy on our squadron, went out there with
Penniston and Burroughs. He didn't believe it. He wanted
to see the indentations. So they took him out there, and
with very little difficulty they found the site. He
scratched his head and said...

Oh! I forgot one thing. The civilian police were called
and were told 'We had something in the forest we couldn't
understand, would they please respond', etc., and they
dispatched two patrolmen. However, they got waylaid by
something more important. There was a fight in a pub and
they never got there.

So there was Captain Verano out there looking with them.
They find the three indentations. He calls the British
police again. Police patrolmen come back out again. They
take a look and their comment is 'Must have been hens
nesting', or something, rabbits burrowing, and they just
glanced at the ground and walked on back to their car and
disappeared.

Well, what are you going to do? Nobody sounds interested

From: "kevin_conde" <kevin_conde@yahoo.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2003 20:22:09 -0000
Subject: [UFORL] Re: Rendlesham Revelations

Robert:

Maj Ed Drury was the operations officer, and Zickler's second in
command. Technically he was the boss of all the working flights.

The individual cops on each LE and security flight worked for either
an NCO under the flight chief or the flight chief himself. The
flight chief reported to the flight commander (Lt. Englund) and the
flight commander reported to the operations officer (Maj Drury), who
reported to Maj Zickler.

Burroughs would only refer to his immediate supervisor or his flight
chief as his "boss". Drury was, in a sense, his boss, but he would
never have referred to him as his boss. The boss, for a normal
flight member, was usually the flight chief. For most of my time I
was a flight chief, and referred to Lt. Englund as my boss.

Just as an aside, it was unusual to have a major and a commander as
both ops officer and commander. As a result Drury and Zickler were
not real popular with each other. Drury wanted to lose Zickler so he
could be the commander, and Zickler did not like Drury always
breathing down his neck waiting for Zickler to screw-up.

Kevin

From: "James Easton" <voyager@jeaston.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2003 23:42:44 +0100
Subject: [UFORL] Rendlesham Revelations

There is some background case material I've become aware
of in recent months and which might be of interest.

Firstly, during December last year, I wrote:

** BEGIN **
In 'Left at East Gate', Warren discusses the February
1985, CNN documentary and how Chuck DeCaro claimed:

"CNN has also found an officer who says he drove the base
commander to a waiting aircraft to deliver what he was
told was a motion-picture film of one of the UFOs".

Warren adds this was, "followed by the officer's
statement. He had been told the film was on its way to
Germany".

If anyone has an available copy of that documentary,
please let me know.

What I do have, courtesy of Greenwood's files, is a
transcript of the CNN program - whether it was the final
version, I'm not certain.

However, it does accordingly state:

"CNN has also found an officer who says he drove the base
commander to a waiting airplane to deliver what he was
told was a motion picture film of one of the UFO's".

The "ANONYMOUS OFFICER" is then quoted:

"...uh, we drove out and I asked him what was in the
film, and he said we actually have pictures of the UFO
here. And he got off the jeep, went over to the aircraft,
handed the film to the pilot. The canopy closed and the
plane took off, and I asked him where it was headed, and
he said, 'Germany'".

There are various tales of 'unscheduled' aircraft,
usually 'cargo flights', arriving on base after the 'UFO
incidents. As Sergeant Randy Smith told me:

"The following night, I went on duty. At guardmount, Bob
Ball was very serious, he's almost never serious, a very
jovial person. He said, 'I saw something last night, but
I'm not at liberty to discuss it'. And that was the
'end'. I later heard that the morning we got off our
first midnight shift, an A-10 was scrambled and sent to
Ramstein, Germany, by Lt. Col. Halt".

So many rumours...


Who was the, as documented within that transcript,
"ANONYMOUS OFFICER" which CNN cited...

In LaEG, Warren talks about the broadcast and how he
recognised aforementioned, 'blacked out' testimony as
originating from Captain Mike Veranno [Verrano?].

I can say, from the transcript, which seems to be
original CNN material _with notes indicating witness
identities_, that every other 'anonymous' witness is
correctly identified by Warren in LaEG.

Annoyingly, I can't say for sure that it was Veranno who
made that claim - it's the one affidavit which isn't
confirmed in CNN's documentation.

However, there is one other CNN "ANONYMOUS OFFICER"
witness statement which - without going into details why
- does seem to be from Veranno.


Yet, Halt confirms:

HALT: There was no video. There was no film taken that
night to my knowledge. Now, it is possible that one of
the young airman, back at a distance because they weren't
allowed to approach close we're talking about the group
that was back at the light-alls... Somebody may have had
a camera back there, but I don't believe so because they
were on duty and they would have had to go through
guardmount. Somebody could have snuck a small, 35mm or
Instamatic or something in their pocket. It's possible
somebody may have had something, but there was no obvious
overt video filming, etc., done that night. None.

RAYL: There was no official video or film taken.

HALT: None. No, nothing official. No.
[END OF EXTRACT]

[...]
As for the assertion that film of our succeeding
Rendlesham forest spaceship was directly transported to
Germany and presumably Ramstein AFB, headquarters of
'United States Air Forces in Europe' [USAFE]... why would
Veranno, or any other "OFFICER" say this?


Note that it was statedly the "base commander" who
carried purported film - the CNN transcript correctly
identifies Halt as "Deputy Base Commander" and any
"OFFICER" should naturally know the difference.

Was therefore Col. Ted Conrad, the 'Base Commander',
involved outwith Halt's knowledge?

It's so untenable that all we seem to be evidencing is
the sheer unreliability of witness testimony...
** END **


In recent discussions with John Burroughs, he brought up
the subject of that CNN documentary, which he
participated in.

To my surprise, John mentioned an argument between Halt
and Veranno, which occurred during the production.

Just before Veranno was about to be filmed, Halt
reportedly took him aside and told him not to make any
claims about transporting evidence to a waiting aircraft.
So far as John was aware, Veranno had "backed down".

I explained how the claim was actually broadcast and
suggested Halt was simply pointing out to Veranno that
there was no such film and he must be mistaken.

Although this was a long time ago now, John's
recollection doesn't agree with my scenario. Reportedly,
Halt had reminded Veranno he [Veranno] was now at the Air
Force Academy and someone in his position shouldn't be
appearing on TV making such statements.

At present, all we can evidently conclude for certain is
that the anonymous officer who appeared in that CNN
documentary was indeed Veranno.


I wonder if he's referring to a separate event - perhaps
at some later date and amidst the 'UFO' hysteria, someone
had filmed what they perceived to be a 'UFO'.
Interestingly, Burroughs recalls that Veranno said it was
the Wing Commander, not the Base Commander, he drove to a
waiting aircraft and perhaps CNN's commentary is in
error.

The Base Commander, Col. Ted Conrad, had remained behind
at the belated officer's Christmas party and delegated
Halt to investigate what was going on during the night of
27 December.

However, the Wing Commander, Col. Gordon Williams, had
taken a great interest in the 'UFO' stories and it was
Williams who took a copy of Halt's microcassette
recording to an already scheduled staff meeting of the
Third Air Force.


One later east gate 'UFO' sighting involved Steve LaPlume
and he described:

OK just to set the time line up a bit: I was stationed at
RAF Bentwaters between Nov. 4th 1980 and April 10,1981. I
had just turned 18 years old in July.

This incident happened about three weeks after the now
infamous Bentwaters sighting/encounter. It was in the 2nd
week of January 1981. I was booted out of the service
almost three months to the day after this event.

RAF Woodbridge is a sister base to RAF Bentwaters. They
are about five miles apart and the 81st Security Police
Squadron which I was attached to covered the security for
both bases. I had not yet received my Secret Clearance
and therefore was temporarily assigned to the Law
Enforcement flight. I worked on one of the flights that
had rotating shifts. three days on swing, three days on
nights and then three days off.

Since I had no clearance I could not go into the Non
Alert Parking Areas (NAPAS) where the A-10's were nor
could I go into the Weapons Storage Area (WSA) which
housed all the ordinance and some small amount of nukes
though I do not know for sure about the nukes.

With all these restrictions I was relegated to sitting
out on the furthermost reaches of our base in a four foot
square cubical and watch the grass grow. For some reason
I got the East gate a lot. Mostly because I was new and
did not really belong to the Law Enforcement (LE) crew. I
did not mind and for the first few months it was OK.

No one bothered me and I could just hang out, check ID's
until the gate closed at about eight o'clock and then
ride shotgun with the shift sergeant. If I was on nights
I would ride with the SGT. first and then be put on the
East gate just before shift change for the morning
traffic. Most of the night was spent relieving other LE
members while they went and ate or took a leak.

On this particular night an airman named Senior Airman
Palmer was on patrol and I was riding along with him. We
went out to check the gate because some people knew the
combination and were using it after hours. I checked to
make sure it was locked. The car was parked back about
fifty feet to help light up the area. The gate was locked
and I went back to the car.

The night was brisk but not cold and SA Palmer and I hung
out leaning against the patrol car and shot the shit for
a while. I was facing south and talking to Palmer who was
facing north. He said " I guess this is where they saw
that UFO a few weeks back." I said "Oh" and asked him
what exactly happened. He did not know for sure but
pointed out a lighthouse way the heck off in the
distance, toward the north sea., and said that they were
saying that was what they saw. I asked about the rumor
that it had been moving through the trees and he just
shrugged "I don't know."

I faced back south after looking east toward the
lighthouse and something caught my eye. Up at cloud level
, which was very high as the night was pretty clear, I
noticed a light moving across the sky. It was like if you
are outside and see a jet off in the distance and while
you can not make out its image you know it's a jet
because it is a small light moving at a steady pace.

This light was not moving at any "pace" it was darting
across the sky very fast. It was up then it was down, up
then down. It probably changed altitude at a difference
of a few thousand feet in elevation ten times in as many
seconds. I simply turned to Palmer and said "huh, that's
different." He looked and spotted it also. We watched it
for about a half a minute or more and he told me to stay
put, that he was going to go to the control tower and see
what was up.

He came back about five minutes later and said they only
had a C-130 and a helicopter up that night and or in this
area. Well I am not a pilot but we both agreed that this
was neither and asked each other if we should call it in.
We agreed that we should. Palmer got on the radio and
announces "La Plume just saw a UFO outside of the East
gate." I cussed him out, what about him he saw it too.

The phone in the security booth rang almost immediately.
I answered it and it was Lt. Englund my shift supervisor.
He wanted to know what exactly I saw and where. I told
him and he ordered me to stay put and keep an eye on it.
The elapse time thus far is approximately fifteen minutes
from the time I first spotted it.

The night was partly cloudy and the craft went behind
some clouds over the Rendlesham forest. It was still at
least fifteen miles away and at an elevation of about
twenty thousand feet or so. It was not like it was
hanging overhead.

Well holy cow the earth opened up and within twenty
minutes I had more people and brass at my post than I had
ever seen. There was the deputy base commander, his wife
and teenage son. They brought along their cameras. I
remember his wife saying something to the effect of "Oh
boy we get to see one". Lt. Englund showed up and told my
not to be nervous that Colonel Williams was on his way
and that he had had just made General. Who me nervous.

I was told to state that my post was "Safe and Secure" I
opened the gate and everyone piled into a blue Air Force
station wagon and a jeep and took off. Palmer and I were
given a night vision scope and told to let them know if
we spotted it again.

We did not look for it much because we figured it was
long gone. I screwed around looking through the N.V.
scope and waited. about an hour later the vehicles came
back and I was told to man the post the rest of the night
and keep them posted if anything happened. They all then
went back to where they came.
[END]


Perhaps a similar incident explains Veranno's claims,
which, understandably, Halt might caution him about
revealing.


James.

From: "Robinson, Larry" <lrobins@indiana.edu>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2003 17:03:31 -0500
Subject: RE: [UFORL] Travis Walton

Again, that depends on the design.

- The tissue paper and tallow Type I can stay lit and aloft over an
hour, as I can personally testify to from a continuous sighting of
two of them.

- The suit bag and birthday candle Type II has a short time of around
10 to 15 minutes, and comes down about 3 to 5 minutes after the
candles extinguish. I have also seen one of these, but it moved out of
sight behind nearby trees within two minutes.

- The large envelope (Saran Wrap, multiple suit bags, or leaf bag) and
church candle Type III can run lit for three or four hours.

- The large envelope and emergency flare Type IV stays lit for 15, 20,
30, or 60 minutes, depending on the flares purchased. The color is
usually red, orange, yellow, or green.

- The gas balloon and emergency flare Type V stays lit the same time as
Type IV, but does not come down afterwards until the balloons lose gas.

Often the lifetime is shorter because something happens to the balloon
before it burns out.

Hi Stephen,

I believe I can answer this one. I tracked down the CO of Eastern
Radar at the time of the incident, Squadron Leader Derek Combe,
do you remember him? (his name appears in the MOD file).

Combe confirmed that he was responsible for impounding the
radar film of the incident[s], after the call from Bentwaters in the
early hours of 28 December 1980. He told me the tapes were
held on the base until early January when a joint RAF-USAF team
from MATO [Military Air Traffic Organisation, RAF Uxbridge]
arrived to collect them. Presumably the tapes were replayed to
check if there was any radar confirmation of the visual sightings -
but bear in mind the checks were based upon the date and times
given in Halt's memo, which were incorrect.

Coumbe says he could only remember one call made to Eastern
Radar, in the early hours of 28 December (this is confirmed by
the base logbook as 0325 hrs), reporting a UFO. This was the
time that Col Halt was leading his expedition into the forest. He
said:

"I recall the incident well...the call came from Bentwaters
RAPcom. They requested that we scan the radars for any
radar targets in the area; there were NONE. They reported
flashing lights in the Rendlesham Forest area, outside the
airfield runway [and that] the base police were investigating
the incident."

The MOD file suggests MATO did check this with the tape,
butthe film was at fault; the memo ends as follows:

"On the night of the reproted sighting our controller on duty
was requested to view the radar; nothing was observed.
The facts are recorded in our log book of that night."
MATO was disbanded in 2000, and we can assume all the
tapes from the time were wiped clean long ago.

best,

Dave Clarke

One. But it was really a bottle rocket fired from the balloon (seen at

craters or the rockets themselves are found). These "rockets" are, of

But to postulate that now, rather than to first look for some
known and mundane cause, is to put the cart before the horse. Look
for the prosaic causes first. They are much more probable than
something "totally different to anything you or I have knowledge
of" is.

It is much more probable that some form of hoax or prank was played,
rather than for a totally new and unknown phenomenon to be present.
If you believe that aliens are more likely than a prank, you need to
rethink the probabilities of events.

And if something had been there, whatever it was STILL had to give
off photons in a direction that entered the eyes of the witnesses, or
they would not have been able to see it. So it must be a phenomenon
which emits a beam or stream of something that then emits light WHILE
it travels.

Possibilities with a probability much higher than space aliens
include:

- Fireworks
- A flame thrower of some sort
- A stream of some kind of dust, illuminated by something like a
  flashlight
- Phosphorescent powder
- Something solid (like a rope or cable) visible only while lit
  by something like a flashlight
- A helicopter with a searchlight - the downwash provided the force
  that knocked Travis over, and raised dust, making the searchlight
  beam visible.

@ it happened and non of his cloths got burnt to my knowledge.
@ "So what kind of light - energy - frequency did this"
@ These are good questions.

This tells me that it was not light that imparted the force.
Electromagnetic waves exert only very minute mechanical force on
objects. Usually when a photon strikes something, it is either
reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through the object. Which one of
the three depends on the frequency of the light and the nature of
what it struck.

If the photon is absorbed, it imparts its energy to the absorbing
material in the form of heat.

Rather, if whatever this was exerted a force, it is likely that the
visible light was a by-product of whatever produced the force, not the
producer of the actual force itself.

@
@ >If Travis was really knocked

@ >that emitted light instead.
@
@ Could it have been static discharge from the object ???

@ got the loader the hum.

That is possible, though at such a range, there would not be much light
from the discharge, and it would be blue, violet, or possibly magenta.
The discharge would have to be over quite a distance before it had
enough
stored energy to make the air incandesce white. Another problem is that
Travis would have had to be closer to the object than a tree or the
ground,
or the discharge would have gone to one of those instead.

Of course, IF there were power lines there, and some implement Travis
had
(such as a thin cable) touched one, it would produce a white display as
the implement vaporized. A hum implies AC power is being expended or a
motor is running.

This is off the track, but it reminds me of quite the oddest non-UFO
case
I ever encountered. At a major university campus (not here), the power
was
shut down over the weekend in one major campus building, to replace the
two
main ground-mount transformers feeding it. One transformer fed the
regular
outlets and lights, the other fed the 277 volt circuits feeding the
large
motors for the air handlers, refrigerant pumps, and condensate pumps.

When the project engineer went into the building after power was
restored,
he turned on the hall lights. All of the fluorescent tubes exploded, and
then the stench of burned out ballasts filled the hall. The cord to an
electric fan burst into flame along its entire length, even though the
fan
was off. Outlet boxes sparked and smoked. Meanwhile, the condensate pump
motors burned out. The entire building hummed and buzzed. The project
engineer said "NO! They DIDN'T! They COULDN'T HAVE! Nobody could be that
STUPID!"

Yep! They DID! The electricians mixed the two transformers up, hooking
the
120 volt transformer to the motor service, and the 277 volt transformer
to
the outlet and lighting service. OOOOOPS!

The reason I brought this up is that an electrical cord catching fire
like
the one in this building could look like a beam, and could knock a guy
flat.

There is one facet that many people seem to forget. If this started out
as a prank or a hoax, and it got out of control when the press took
over,
the hoaxters cannot come forward without facing criminal charges for
false reporting or perjury. Most counties, after expending money
investigating such cases, would file charges just to recover the money
they spent, through the fines they would collect if the perpetrator
pleads
guilty. This leaves the perpetrator with a criminal record.

From: "Stephen" <trinderbrook@hotmail.com>

Subject: [UFORL] Rendlesham Incident

I have read with interest many records of the tapes being taken from
Eastern Radar three weeks after the event by MOD persons or Usafe
persons.

This would relate to the radio tapes i.e. 16 track voice recorders
which were normally held for enquiry purposes by the Airworks
technicians.

Having been at ER from 1982 to 1985 it was common knowledge that the
Radar Picture was recorded on 16mm film - a medium that was not
subject to re-recording (Video not being available at that time).

These films were stored daily. The ones in question were still
available to view well into 82/83.

A Japanese TV crew did arrange to see them officially and only then
was it discovered that the dates in question had been removed. It was
confirmed that at no time had MOD/USAFE investigators had access to
these film cans, which meant that someone within Eastern Radar had
removed them.

Only one American Senior officer worked at ER during this time and
had just recently been promoted and posted to Upper Heyford as SATCO
prior to the discovery that the film of the incident was missing.

It is possible that he was either struck by lightning, or by some

@ The guys said the light coming from the object was so intense
@ it was blinding.

I have at least 6 KNOWN fire balloon cases in my files where the
witness described the light as "blinding". It would be blinding to a
dark-adapted eye.

Most people are surprised at the fact that most human senses have
"automatic gain control" systems that slowly raise or lower sensitivity
to match the environment and get the best use of the sense. Both the
human ear and the human eye have a sensitivity range of power levels
over a range of 1 to 1000000000000 (that's 10^12, or 1 trillion US, or 1
billion UK). But that range includes the complete span of the automatic
gain adjustment too. In any one environment (or if the automatic gain
system is not working), the range is closer to 1 to 100000 (that's 10^5,
or 100 thousand).

So a light that seems miniscule in a daylight environment seems
blinding if the witness has been in total darkness for half an hour or
more. It takes about a minute for the automatic gain of the eye to turn
down, and about half an hour for the automatic gain to turn up.

One way to witness this is to wake up in the middle of the night where
there is no traffic outside. You hear a loud thump, thump, thump. Then
you realize that it is the ticking of that battery wall clock with
hands. Your ears were cranked all the way up. Then the light that
dazzles you when you open your eyes is the green "standby" light on
your VCR. Your eyes were cranked too. Turn on a radio and the room
light, and at first, they seem ultra-powerful. But within a minute,
they seem normal. Now shut off the radio and light, and you barely
notice the ticking clock or the VCR light. Now your senses are turned
down.

@ >In this case, the human eye needed a medium (dust, smoke,
@ >water vapor) to be seen by the woodcutters, who didn't have
@ >an equiped physics laboratory to see light waves travelling
@ >through a vacuum.

This is most likely a typo, and should read:

@ >In this case, the light beam needed a medium (dust, smoke,
@ >water vapor) to be seen by the woodcutters

@ Why

Because, unless it collides with something, a photon always travels in
a straight line. A photon would have to strike something in order to be
turned in a different direction, so it can enter the eye of the witness
sideways to the beam. If no photons are deflected in the direction of
the witness, then no light enters the eye of the witness from the beam,
and so the witness can't see the beam. All the witness would see of the
beam would be the spot where the beam strikes something.

@>
@ >> Larry, list has anyone ever thought of analysing the
@ colour of the light
@ >> beam that was said to have struck Travis that was witnessed by
@ >> the witnesses.?
@ >> If not why not? the colour of the light might able to
@ determine the
@ >> frequency used to knock Travis on his backside.?
@
@ The colour white-ish like molten metal

That's the one color that does not tell you anything. White is a mixture
of many different frequencies, like a rushing sound ("white noise") is a
mixture of many different frequencies of sound. The only light I know of
that can move something is coherent (LASER) light, and coherent light
must be a pure spectral color. Any mixture of frequencies can not
possibly be coherent.

I still don't think that light could exert enough force to move a person
without first setting his clothes on fire. If Travis was really knocked
down, I don't think it was light that did it. It had to be something
that emitted light instead.

Like a skyrocket. The blast behind it emits light, and a large one could
knock a person over. But if the payload exploded normally, Travis would
have had extensive burn injuries. So it would have to have been a
different
sort of rocket (such as a model rocket). Either the rocket cartridge or
the rocket blast is capable of knocking someone over.

@ >The frequency, of course, was determined by the woodcutters in
@ >their equipped physics lab, after they stopped running for
@ their lives.

I always carry a diffraction grating in my wallet for just this kind of
emergency.

List:

I don't know anything about this case, but I am a cop. RE:

>Oh? The police go nuts whenever an auto accident or a robbery >occurs, because
they get so many different versions of what >happened and what kinds of cars and
people were involved. But >the police routinely keep the witnesses separated before
they >interview them, to keep them from affecting each other's >accounts. The fact
that the witnesses to this UFO agree on what >they saw suggests to me that they
discussed it among themselves >before the interviews (or possibly that they agreed to
a >description in advance).

Unless I arrive onscene immediately, and can verify that my witnesses have not had a
chance to discuss what they saw, I tend to be suspicious when multiple witnesses give
me identical stories. If the stories are essentially the same, yet told differently,
meaning they use their own unique wording, descriptions, and phrases, I tend to
accept the story. I love these types of witness statements as they tend to be accurate.

When not only the kernal of the story is the same, but the words, descriptions and
phrasings tend to be the same, my assumption is they have discussed the incident
prior to my arrival. These types of statements are problematic. It doesn't mean they
are wrong, but they can present problems as time goes by. In 5 or 10 years can we be
sure they are telling us what they saw, or what the they think they saw based on what
everyone else was saying.

Someone more familiar with this case would have to compare the witness statements
and ask are the stories different in wording and phrasing, yet essentially the same, or
are the stories the same in content as well as delivery?

Kevin

Actually, Edmund Scientific used to sell a tissue paper hot air
balloon kit that is remarkably similar in size and shape to the object
pictured on the cover of the book. It even came with the letters "U",
"F", and "O", which could be applied to the balloon. The heading in
the catalog said: "Make and fly your own UFO." This kit was designed
to be heated from the ground with a hair dryer (not taking any power
source aloft, for fire safety). But add the fire balloon candle motor
and you have a rather hazardous fire balloon.

The Edmund balloon has been confirmed to be the cause of one case in
Texas during the big 1973 flap. When asked how she knew the object
was a UFO, the witness replied: "It said "UFO" right on the side.

------

The picture on the book also looks like a silkspan flying saucer we
made in 1965 in my model airplane club. It had a model airplane engine
in a ducted fan configuration through the center, and ribbed panels
out to the rim. But it didn't work right. Instead of hovering like a
UFO, it flipped on edge, fell to the ground, and then, powered by the
torque from the engine and propeller, took off rolling on its rim at
about 40 miles per hour across the football field we were using for
an airport. It finally crashed in some bushes.

 -----Original Message-----
 From: Robinson, Larry [mailto:lrobins@indiana.edu]

 I didn't say it WAS a fire balloon. I'm saying that what the other
 workers saw had no reported characteristics that could refute a fire
 balloon.

 But one thing really conflicts with the story - the "beam" they say
 they saw strike Travis. This is not indicative of an energy weapon of
 some kind, but of science fiction. Such beams appear only as special
 effects in Hollywodd productions, or as part of a light beam seen in
 in fog or dust. Notice that a LASER pointer does NOT betray its
 location in the air as a beam, but appears only where it strikes.
 Even in fog, I cannot see the beam of my LASER pointer. Possible
 causes of a visible beam of light include:

 - Fireworks of some kind.

 - A focused light source, combined with dust, smoke, or fog.

 - A stream of flowing matter (such as water).

 - A cable, rope, or other long thin object illuminated by an external
 light source.

 Note that only the part of a searchlight beam that is pointed away
 from you is visible as a beam, except when the air has a lot of dust
 or fog in it. The visibility of the beam pointed away from you is
 caused by the extremely large amount of air illuminated by the beam
 and overlapping at the same place in your visual field, backscattering
 enough light to be seen. But at right angles to the beam, the amount
 of illuminated air at any one point in your visual field is too small
 to normally be invisible.

@ Light waves do not need a medium to travel through.

@ A light wave consists of energy in the form of electric and
@ magnetic fields.
@ The fields vibrate at right angles to the direction of
@ movement of the wave,
@ and at right angles to each other. Because light has both
@ electric and
@ magnetic fields, it is also referred to as electromagnetic radiation.
@
@ Light waves come in many frequencies.
@ The frequency is the number of waves that pass a point in space
@ during any time interval, usually one second.
@ It is measured in units of cycles (waves) per second, or Hertz (Hz).
@ The frequency
@ of visible light is referred to as color, and ranges from 430
@ trillion Hz, seen as

@ frequencies extends
@ beyond the visible spectrum, from less than one billion Hz, as in
@ radio waves, to
@ greater than 3 billion billion Hz, as in gamma rays.

of space caused by intense gravity.

@ of energy in

Larry no! science has found that light can be manipulated and light can be
slowed down. Larry can you look outside of your box for a moment and
start looking at the findings of science and not Hollywood. <smile>

Light how it works

Light waves do not need a medium to travel through.
Light waves can travel through a vacuum.
A light wave consists of energy in the form of electric and magnetic fields.
The fields vibrate at right angles to the direction of movement of the wave,
and at right angles to each other. Because light has both electric and
magnetic fields, it is also referred to as electromagnetic radiation.

Light waves come in many frequencies.
The frequency is the number of waves that pass a point in space
during any time interval, usually one second.
It is measured in units of cycles (waves) per second, or Hertz (Hz).
The frequency
of visible light is referred to as color, and ranges from 430
trillion Hz, seen as
red, to 750 trillion Hz, seen as violet. Again, the full range of
frequencies extends
beyond the visible spectrum, from less than one billion Hz, as in
radio waves, to
greater than 3 billion billion Hz, as in gamma rays.

As noted above, light waves are waves of energy. The amount of energy in
a light wave is proportionally related to its frequency: High frequency light
has high energy; low frequency light has low energy. Thus gamma rays
have the most energy, and radio waves have the least. Of visible light,
violet has the most energy and red the least.

Larry, list has anyone ever thought of analysing the colour of the light beam
that was said to have struck Travis that was witnessed by the witnesses.?
If not why not? the colour of the light might able to determine the frequency
used to knock Travis on his backside.?
-----

Light not only vibrates at different frequencies, it also travels at different
  speeds. Light waves move through a vacuum at their maximum speed,
300,000 kilometers per second or 186,000 miles per second, which
makes light the fastest phenomenon in the universe. Light waves slow
down when they travel inside substances, such as air, water, glass or a
diamond. The way different substances affect the speed at which light
travels is key to understanding the bending of light, or refraction.

More at this page:
source: How Light Works
by Craig Freudenrich, Ph.D.
http://science.howstuffworks.com/light4.htm

"A new witness I recently located is Mike Jenkins, who

and then moved to 'Bentwaters Missile Maintenance'. Mike
has a strange tale to tell and which he dates as
occurring during some 'UFO' excitement, specifically the
morning after 'Lt. Col. Halt went out on the night
shift'.

He recalls:

'When I came in the next morning, all I saw was a lot of
our staff in uniform and in civilian dress, posted about
the weapons storage area, and everyone being told to not
ask questions, just do our jobs. To me it appeared to be
no more than a regular training or alert drill after
which there is normally a higher level of visible
security at the twin bases anyway'."

Subject: [UFORL] List 'housekeeping rules'

This is due for an update.

Confirmation of the list 'housekeeping rules':

1. The UFO Research List [UFORL] is open to subscription from
those who advocate and adopt a consistent, scientific appraisal
of purported 'UFO' related evidence. The remit encompasses
associated topics which may be relevant, such as 'black
projects', or 'ball lightning', etc.

The list is moderated and currently has over 180 subscribers.

Your subscription e-mail address will be visible to all other
subscribers.


2. The list archives are *PUBLIC* and the forum is *NOT* intended
to enable secure discussions, although due copyright applies to
any subscriber's contributions. Particular care should be taken
when posting material which may be copyrighted. A suggested
approach would be, 'if in doubt, leave it out'.

Discussion archives are publicly available at URL:

http://groups.yahoo.com/group/UFORL/messages


3. The UFORL 'home page' is located on the Internet at URL:

http://groups.yahoo.com/group/UFORL

This provides access to the public list postings, plus the
addresses for subscribe or unsubscribe requests.


4. The list address for mail is:

UFORL@yahoogroups.com

With some e-mail software, using 'reply' may not send a response
to the list, it will be sent ONLY to the address shown in the
'From' heading, which is the person who sent the mail.

It's recommended that the destination of your reply is therefore
checked before sending and should always be as above.
5. The standard mailing list code applies and messages should be
unformatted, in plain text and no more than 65 characters in
length.

PLEASE NOTE: If replying to mail, only the relevant section(s)
should be quoted, not the entire original message.


6. As a security precaution, e-mail attachments should *NEVER* be
sent to the list - they will be removed automatically. Members
can upload files to the UFORL library area, at:

http://groups.yahoo.com/group/UFORL/files/


7. Postings should not be anonymous and the sender's name is
expected to be contained either in the heading or signature.


8. Strict 'Netiquette' rules apply and all postings are expected
to be cordial, ensuring the list is always a pleasant
environment.

For further information see:

http://www.albion.com/netiquette/corerules.html


Any related problems or queries should be addressed to:

UFORL-owner@yahoogroups.com


James Easton,
List Owner.

From: "Robinson, Larry" <lrobins@indiana.edu>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2003 13:31:10 -0500
Subject: RE: [UFORL] Travis Walton

I didn't say it WAS a fire balloon. I'm saying that what the other
workers saw had no reported characteristics that could refute a fire
balloon.

But one thing really conflicts with the story - the "beam" they say
they saw strike Travis. This is not indicative of an energy weapon of
some kind, but of science fiction. Such beams appear only as special
effects in Hollywodd productions, or as part of a light beam seen in
in fog or dust. Notice that a LASER pointer does NOT betray its
location in the air as a beam, but appears only where it strikes.
Even in fog, I cannot see the beam of my LASER pointer. Possible
causes of a visible beam of light include:

- Fireworks of some kind.

- A focused light source, combined with dust, smoke, or fog.

- A stream of flowing matter (such as water).

- A cable, rope, or other long thin object illuminated by an external
light source.

Note that only the part of a searchlight beam that is pointed away
from you is visible as a beam, except when the air has a lot of dust
or fog in it. The visibility of the beam pointed away from you is
caused by the extremely large amount of air illuminated by the beam
and overlapping at the same place in your visual field, backscattering
enough light to be seen. But at right angles to the beam, the amount
of illuminated air at any one point in your visual field is too small
to normally be invisible.

From: "Robinson, Larry" <lrobins@indiana.edu>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2003 13:31:10 -0500
Subject: RE: [UFORL] Travis Walton

I didn't say it WAS a fire balloon. I'm saying that what the other
workers saw had no reported characteristics that could refute a fire
balloon.

But one thing really conflicts with the story - the "beam" they say
they saw strike Travis. This is not indicative of an energy weapon of
some kind, but of science fiction. Such beams appear only as special
effects in Hollywodd productions, or as part of a light beam seen in
in fog or dust. Notice that a LASER pointer does NOT betray its
location in the air as a beam, but appears only where it strikes.
Even in fog, I cannot see the beam of my LASER pointer. Possible
causes of a visible beam of light include:

- Fireworks of some kind.

- A focused light source, combined with dust, smoke, or fog.

- A stream of flowing matter (such as water).

- A cable, rope, or other long thin object illuminated by an external
light source.

Note that only the part of a searchlight beam that is pointed away
from you is visible as a beam, except when the air has a lot of dust
or fog in it. The visibility of the beam pointed away from you is
caused by the extremely large amount of air illuminated by the beam
and overlapping at the same place in your visual field, backscattering
enough light to be seen. But at right angles to the beam, the amount
of illuminated air at any one point in your visual field is too small
to normally be invisible.

From: "Robert Mclean" <robert.mclean2@virgin.net>

Subject: Re: [UFORL] Nick Pope on Rendlesham

<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Hi All</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Since Nick Pope raises some
pertinent&nbsp;questions, I thought I should go on the record regarding various
aspects of the BBC Inside Out documentary.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Back in April 2001, I helped establish the location
of Kevin Conde's hoax, prank, or whatever you want to call it. When sent a map,
Kevin originally thought that the location was inside the security fencing,
about 80 or 90 m west and a little bit south of the East Gate Guard House, at
the point where the outer security fencing takes a bend to the south. I went out
to look at the location, and there were no berms or other walls earthworks at
that location. That location is also inside an inner security fence that extends
around the hardened aircraft bunkers. I don't know for sure that the inner
security fence was there in 1980, but it is there in a 1986 aerial
photo.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>There are some small buildings between the
location
Kevin initially identified and the then East Gate Guard House (the present Guard
House is not the one they had in 1980), which could have provided cover for
Kevin's Hoax. But after correspondence,&nbsp;and having seen emailed photos and
the 1986 aerial photo, Kevin agreed with my suggestion that it was more likely
that his prank was conducted behind the cover of the Blast Wall, which runs an
east-west direction for roughly 75 m just to the west of the East Gate Guard
House, separating the road that leads to the Gate from a large paved taxiway
just to the north. The Blast wall protects anything and anyone&nbsp;on the road
at the Guard House from the blast of the jets as they turn towards the
runway.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Because the location of Kevin's Hoax is essentially
west of the East Gate Guard House, there has never been any doubt that his prank
could&nbsp; ** not **&nbsp;have been connected in any way with lights seen on
the first night (early hours of 26 Dec. 1980) by Steffens, Burroughs, Penniston
and Cabansag, which of course were seen to the east of East Gate. Furthermore,
the whole point of Kevin's prank was to frighten the inexperienced guard posted
at East Gate, and we know that there was no guard posted at East Gate in the
early hours of 26 Dec 1980, as that is why Burroughs and Steffens had to go
there in their car - to check the security of the gate.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>The question then becomes whether or not Kevin's
prank could have taken place on one of the subsequent nights, and no doubt this
debate will rage for some time. I will keep an open mind on this until evidence
appears one way or the other. However, I am certain that Lt Col Halt on the
night of 28 December 1980 could not have seen lights from Kevin's prank, because
he was simply too far away from the scene of this hoax. Lt Col Halt's party
started off near the eastern edge of Rendlesham forest, and then headed east
after a flashing light was spotted. They ended up in the "second farmer's
field". By deducing which terrestrial lights Col Halt was following, I believe
this to be Burrow Hill. Brenda Butler had previously come to the same
conclusion, because Col Halt described to her the view he had from this hill as
he looked south towards the sea along the line of the Butley River, which he
recalled seeing in the moonlight.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Burrow Hill is over 4 km from East Gate. In
between
is Oak Wood - a substantial wood about 500 m across. Even if all the trees in
Rendlesham forest had been cut down by late Dec 1980, there is simply no way
Halt could have seen any lights near ground level at East Gate from Burrow Hill,
given the distance involved and the obstruction of the trees in Oak Wood -
certainly not coloured flashlights pointed up.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>If we assume that Kevin's Hoax did take place in
the early hours of 28 Dec. 1980, then it is possible that someone nearer his
Hoax might have seen the lights - possibly even someone in the WSA Guard Tower
at Bentwaters, which has a good view to the south.&nbsp;It is possible that the
frightened guard got on his radio and spread the story. It is conceivable that
somehow this got relayed by radio to Lt Col Halt while he was on Burrow Hill,
and that this might be the source of his tales of lights "beaming down" on the
base. But these are a lot of ifs, and it would still be an amazing coincidence
if Kevin's Hoax had accidentally taken place on the same night that Halt was out
on his expedition, with there being no other connection between these events.
It's not impossible, but you have to ask yourself what are the odds if there is
no underlying connection between these events. Of course, there may be some
connection, but if so we don't know what it is.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>I met with the producer of the BBC Inside Out
show,
Mr Clive Dunn for about 4 hours a couple of weeks before they shot the scenes in
Rendlesham forest. Going over maps, I explained to him the reasons why Kevin's
Hoax could not explain either the lights seen on the first night, or the lights
to the east which Lt Col Halt followed or those viewed from Burrow Hill. I told
him that in my opinion the only possible connection was with reports that lights
had "beamed down" on the base, but as yet there was no&nbsp;real evidence to tie
the two together. Of course, the reports of lights beaming down has only ever
been a very minor part of the story, and I don't think many researchers have
ever taken this very seriously.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>I know some people have heaped praise on the
BBC
documentary, and I suppose they must be due some credit for not simply rehashing
the somewhat incredible stories that typically have formed the bulk of previous
TV documentaries on the Rendlesham Incidents. Allowances must be made for the
fact that had a very limited budget compared with earlier documentaries, and
only 7 to 9 minutes of available airtime. But my heart still sank when I saw the
Inside Out show. I knew that they had overplayed the story, and that there would
be a barrage of attacks on those involved, despite some&nbsp;solid skeptical
evidence they aired, particularly from John Burroughs. These weaknesses have
been spotted and have overshadowed the more solid parts of the show. I feel
particularly sorry that Kevin Conde has had to bear some of the heat, as
he&nbsp;didn't have to stick his neck out. I discussed his recollections
personally with him at length while he was over here, and&nbsp;I'm convinced he
is telling the truth.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>The responsibility for "sexing up" Kevin's story
belongs with the BBC, not Kevin.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>And that's the first and last time I'm going to
make any comments on the BBC Inside Out show.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Best regards</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Robert McLean</FONT></DIV>

<BR>accompanied while he carried out his practical joke (I do not <BR>believe
that any names or other details have been given). He <BR>stated that he would
only have been accompanied during an <BR>exercise or alert. So that looked
like case closed, because <BR>there wasn't an alert or exercise at the time of
the UFO <BR>incidents. Conde was honest enough to tell Easton he'd made a
<BR>mistake, and that his prank could have had nothing to do with <BR>the
case.<BR><BR>But then Easton remembered something he'd seen in Peter Robbins
<BR>and Larry Warren's book, Left At East Gate. One of the <BR>photographs in
the book is a picture Larry claimed to have taken <BR>on the morning of
December 28, 1980. It was a picture of the <BR>main gate at RAF Bentwaters. A
sign was clearly visible, on <BR>which the words "Alert Condition" could be
seen. Easton told <BR>Conde about this, and Conde then changed his mind,
saying this <BR>showed he could have been present during the UFO incidents,
and <BR>that his alleged prank might therefore still explain some part <BR>of
what took place.<BR><BR>I believe that all this was based on a
misunderstanding, because <BR>the bottom of the sign is obscured. Actually,
the sign will not <BR>have said "Alert Condition" only. Underneath the words
"Alert <BR>Condition" would have been a descriptor of what the Alert
<BR>Condition actually was (MOD establishments use ones such as <BR>"Black",
 "Black Special" etc). To be fair, this isn't something <BR>I would expect
 Easton to have know. But I'm surprised Conde <BR>didn't pick it
 up.<BR><BR>Taking the above into account, there's now no evidence that
 <BR>there was any exercise or alert at the time of the UFO <BR>sightings.
 Seeing as Conde has said his prank took place during <BR>an exercise or alert,
 this seems to make it abundantly clear <BR>that Conde could have had
 absolutely nothing to do with the UFO <BR>sightings.<BR><BR>I wonder if
Conde
 will now rethink his position, and realise <BR>that his doubts that he was
 responsible were correct, after all.<BR><BR><BR>Best wishes,<BR><BR>Nick
Pope

From: "Robert Mclean" <robert.mclean2@virgin.net>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2003 22:44:57 +0100
Subject: Re: [UFORL] Nick Pope on Rendlesham

<BODY bgColor=#ffffff>


<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Hi All</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Since Nick Pope raises some
pertinent&nbsp;questions, I thought I should go on the record regarding various
aspects of the BBC Inside Out documentary.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Back in April 2001, I helped establish the location
of Kevin Conde's hoax, prank, or whatever you want to call it. When sent a map,
Kevin originally thought that the location was inside the security fencing,
about 80 or 90 m west and a little bit south of the East Gate Guard House, at
the point where the outer security fencing takes a bend to the south. I went out
to look at the location, and there were no berms or other walls earthworks at
that location. That location is also inside an inner security fence that extends
around the hardened aircraft bunkers. I don't know for sure that the inner
security fence was there in 1980, but it is there in a 1986 aerial
photo.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>There are some small buildings between the
location
Kevin initially identified and the then East Gate Guard House (the present Guard
House is not the one they had in 1980), which could have provided cover for
Kevin's Hoax. But after correspondence,&nbsp;and having seen emailed photos and
the 1986 aerial photo, Kevin agreed with my suggestion that it was more likely
that his prank was conducted behind the cover of the Blast Wall, which runs an
east-west direction for roughly 75 m just to the west of the East Gate Guard
House, separating the road that leads to the Gate from a large paved taxiway
just to the north. The Blast wall protects anything and anyone&nbsp;on the road
at the Guard House from the blast of the jets as they turn towards the
runway.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Because the location of Kevin's Hoax is essentially
west of the East Gate Guard House, there has never been any doubt that his prank
could&nbsp; ** not **&nbsp;have been connected in any way with lights seen on
the first night (early hours of 26 Dec. 1980) by Steffens, Burroughs, Penniston
and Cabansag, which of course were seen to the east of East Gate. Furthermore,
the whole point of Kevin's prank was to frighten the inexperienced guard posted
at East Gate, and we know that there was no guard posted at East Gate in the
early hours of 26 Dec 1980, as that is why Burroughs and Steffens had to go
there in their car - to check the security of the gate.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>The question then becomes whether or not Kevin's
prank could have taken place on one of the subsequent nights, and no doubt this
debate will rage for some time. I will keep an open mind on this until evidence
appears one way or the other. However, I am certain that Lt Col Halt on the
night of 28 December 1980 could not have seen lights from Kevin's prank, because
he was simply too far away from the scene of this hoax. Lt Col Halt's party
started off near the eastern edge of Rendlesham forest, and then headed east
after a flashing light was spotted. They ended up in the "second farmer's
field". By deducing which terrestrial lights Col Halt was following, I believe
this to be Burrow Hill. Brenda Butler had previously come to the same
conclusion, because Col Halt described to her the view he had from this hill as
he looked south towards the sea along the line of the Butley River, which he
recalled seeing in the moonlight.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Burrow Hill is over 4 km from East Gate. In
between
is Oak Wood - a substantial wood about 500 m across. Even if all the trees in
Rendlesham forest had been cut down by late Dec 1980, there is simply no way
Halt could have seen any lights near ground level at East Gate from Burrow Hill,
given the distance involved and the obstruction of the trees in Oak Wood -
certainly not coloured flashlights pointed up.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>If we assume that Kevin's Hoax did take place in
the early hours of 28 Dec. 1980, then it is possible that someone nearer his
Hoax might have seen the lights - possibly even someone in the WSA Guard Tower
at Bentwaters, which has a good view to the south.&nbsp;It is possible that the
frightened guard got on his radio and spread the story. It is conceivable that
somehow this got relayed by radio to Lt Col Halt while he was on Burrow Hill,
and that this might be the source of his tales of lights "beaming down" on the
base. But these are a lot of ifs, and it would still be an amazing coincidence
if Kevin's Hoax had accidentally taken place on the same night that Halt was out
on his expedition, with there being no other connection between these events.
It's not impossible, but you have to ask yourself what are the odds if there is
no underlying connection between these events. Of course, there may be some
connection, but if so we don't know what it is.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>I met with the producer of the BBC Inside Out
show,
Mr Clive Dunn for about 4 hours a couple of weeks before they shot the scenes in
Rendlesham forest. Going over maps, I explained to him the reasons why Kevin's
Hoax could not explain either the lights seen on the first night, or the lights
to the east which Lt Col Halt followed or those viewed from Burrow Hill. I told
him that in my opinion the only possible connection was with reports that lights
had "beamed down" on the base, but as yet there was no&nbsp;real evidence to tie
the two together. Of course, the reports of lights beaming down has only ever
been a very minor part of the story, and I don't think many researchers have
ever taken this very seriously.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>I know some people have heaped praise on the
BBC
documentary, and I suppose they must be due some credit for not simply rehashing
the somewhat incredible stories that typically have formed the bulk of previous
TV documentaries on the Rendlesham Incidents. Allowances must be made for the
fact that had a very limited budget compared with earlier documentaries, and
only 7 to 9 minutes of available airtime. But my heart still sank when I saw the
Inside Out show. I knew that they had overplayed the story, and that there would
be a barrage of attacks on those involved, despite some&nbsp;solid skeptical
evidence they aired, particularly from John Burroughs. These weaknesses have
been spotted and have overshadowed the more solid parts of the show. I feel
particularly sorry that Kevin Conde has had to bear some of the heat, as
he&nbsp;didn't have to stick his neck out. I discussed his recollections
personally with him at length while he was over here, and&nbsp;I'm convinced he
is telling the truth.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>The responsibility for "sexing up" Kevin's story
belongs with the BBC, not Kevin.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>And that's the first and last time I'm going to
make any comments on the BBC Inside Out show.</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Best regards</FONT></DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV><FONT face=Arial size=2>Robert McLean</FONT></DIV>

late. 'A' Flight relieved us at 9:30 am, very late.

When we went out the East gate back to Bentwaters,
leaving Woodbridge, there were many people, including
numerous people in typical lab coats making an analysis
of the area.. You could see out the vehicle to the right
side, that there were many people examining the area,
searching, looking for something. Some of these people
were in white overcoats, that's why I say that they
looked like typical techs in lab coats.

This link confirms the information I had informally: that in
June 1964 Bawdsey lost its Master Radar station status and
became a satellite station feeding Neatishead.

In March 1975 Bawdsey closed and was placed on care and
maintenance status: it's radars were dismantled and removed
in 1977.

The station re-opened in August 1979 as a Bloodhound
surface to air missile base.

This suggests to me that if the UFO incident was reported
to Bawdsey then it was simply because this was nearest
RAF base. Perhaps there was an RAF intelligence officer
there who acted as a channel between USAF and RAF.
But either way, Bawdsey would not have been tracking
UFOs on radar in 1980!

Quoting John Burroughs:

> As far as Halt goes, he stated that US AF went to the
> British site and took all of the radar tapes. I'm not
> sure where Bawdsey came up, all I know was that it was
> taken from the eastern radar site and Bawdsey was named
> as that site...

This myth originated with Jenny Randles' informant at
RAF Watton and is repeated over and over again.
I have published the testimony of Sqn Leader Coumbe
of RAF Watton who says it was he who impounded the
radar tapes and notified RAF Fighter Command.
The tapes were removed by a joint RAF/USAF team
from MATO for analysis in January 1980. Coumbe says
there was nothing unusual about this procedure, it was
standard. However, civilian ATC controllers at Watton
appear to have been told the tapes were being confiscated
and there had been a UFO landing in Rendlesham forest
etc.
>
> Leaving aside whether RAF Bawdsey actually had any
